title: Personal Website Revamp — Single-page Next.js rebuild

source.priorRepoHistory: The previous Next.js multi-page site (/, /about, /projects, /tools) was deleted in commit 5eb8899 ("cleanup"). Its source is still recoverable via `git show b5e4821:<path>` (last commit before cleanup) and is a useful reference for existing conventions, project data/SVGs, and package versions — but the new build is single-page per README.md, and /tools is dropped entirely.

summary: Rebuild silviorodrigues.dev as a single scrolling page (hero, filterable Writing/Projects feed, newsletter signup) with a git-based MDX blog, replacing the deleted multi-page Next.js site. Stack: Next.js App Router with static export, Tailwind, MDX content, Resend newsletter via a separate Cloudflare Worker, deployed to GitHub Pages via Actions. Full details, design tokens, and copy are in README.md; pixel reference and mock interactivity are in Personal-Website.dc.html (a design reference only — not to be copied verbatim).

userStories.title: Project scaffold: Next.js + Tailwind + static export
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a working Next.js App Router project configured for static export with Tailwind and the site's design tokens, so later stories have a buildable foundation.
acceptanceCriteria: package.json, tsconfig.json, next.config.js (output: 'export'), tailwind.config.ts, postcss.config.js, .eslintrc.json, .editorconfig, .gitignore restored/recreated (reference old versions via `git show b5e4821:<path>`, e.g. next.config.js needs output:'export' added which the old one didn't have)

Tailwind config / globals.css encode the Design Tokens from README.md: background #171717 (page) / #1c1c1c (cards), borders #262626 / hover #404040, text #fafafa/#e5e5e5/#a3a3a3/#737373/#525252, accent #6dd5ed, gradient #2193b0→#6dd5ed→#6dd5ed→#2193b0 with the `shine` keyframe animation (reuse the existing `linear-wipe` CSS from the old globals.css, retrievable via `git show b5e4821:src/app/globals.css`), radii (10-12px cards/inputs, 999px pills, 50% avatar), selection color #2193b0 bg / #fafafa text
Raleway (400/500/600/700/800) loaded via Google Fonts (or next/font/google) and set as the base font
public/images/profile-picture.png present (copy from assets/profile-picture.png at repo root)
`npm install` and `npm run build` succeed with a placeholder homepage

userStories.title: Header and Footer components
userStories.description: As a visitor, I want a sticky header with nav and a consistent footer, so I can navigate the single page and reach my contact links from anywhere.
acceptanceCriteria: Sticky header: backdrop-filter blur(10px), background rgba(23,23,23,.82), bottom border 1px solid #262626
Header left: home icon SVG (currentColor) linking to #top; reuse the icon path from the old src/components/header.tsx (`git show b5e4821:src/components/header.tsx`)
Header right: nav links 'Writing' (#work), 'Contact' (#subscribe); pill hover state background #262626, color #fafafa, border-radius 8px
Footer: centered icon row (mail via mailto:hi@silviorodrigues.dev, LinkedIn, GitHub) reusing SVGs/links from old src/components/footer.tsx; '© 2026 Silvio Rodrigues' at 12.5px, #525252
LinkedIn/GitHub links open in a new tab

userStories.title: Hero section (#top)
userStories.description: As a visitor, I want a hero section that introduces Silvio, so I immediately understand who he is and how to reach him.
acceptanceCriteria: 84x84 circular avatar using public/images/profile-picture.png, 2px border #262626
Gradient H1 'Silvio Rodrigues' using the linear-wipe/shine treatment, clamp(34px,6vw,52px)
Bold 18px white role line: 'Staff Software Engineer @ KOHO' with KOHO linking to koho.ca (new tab)
Muted 16px line: 'part-time builder, writing about design systems, front-end and AI 🧪'
CTA row: solid pill 'Say hi 👋' linking to mailto:hi@silviorodrigues.dev, plus LinkedIn and GitHub icon links (new tab)
Section is anchored at id="top"

userStories.title: Projects data and filter chips
userStories.description: As a visitor, I want to filter between Writing and Projects and see project cards, so I can browse only what I'm interested in.
acceptanceCriteria: Section #work with gradient H2 'Writing & projects 🧪'
Filter chip row: All / Writing / Projects as a client component with local state ('all'|'writing'|'projects'), not persisted, no navigation
Active chip: solid #fafafa background, #171717 text; inactive: transparent background, 1px solid #333, #a3a3a3 text

Projects cluster: two static cards — alugaTI and Front In Vale — using the inline SVG logos and copy from the old src/data/projects.ts (`git show b5e4821:src/data/projects.ts`), each with name, description, 'Visit site →' external link (new tab); Front In Vale additionally shows a '3k+ people impacted' pill badge
Toggling the chips shows/hides the Writing and/or Projects clusters accordingly (Writing cluster can be a placeholder until US-5 wires real posts in)

userStories.title: MDX blog pipeline and Writing cluster
userStories.description: As Silvio, I want to write posts as MDX files with frontmatter, so I can publish new writing via git without a CMS.
acceptanceCriteria: content/posts/*.mdx files with frontmatter: title, date, tag, excerpt, readMins
Parsing via gray-matter; a lib module lists all posts sorted newest-first and exposes slug + frontmatter
At least one seed MDX post exists so the feed is populated

Writing cluster (inside #work, wired into the filter chips from US-4) renders one card per post: tag pill (color #6dd5ed, background rgba(109,213,237,.12)), date + read time (muted, 12px), title (bold 17px), excerpt (14.5px, #a3a3a3), 'Read post →' (#6dd5ed)
Clicking a Writing card navigates to its post route (implemented in US-6)

userStories.title: Post detail route (/blog/[slug])
userStories.description: As a visitor, I want to read a full post on its own page, so I can consume the content and share a direct link.
acceptanceCriteria: Route at /blog/[slug], statically generated at build time from the MDX files (generateStaticParams), rendered with next-mdx-remote or @next/mdx
'← Back' control, tag + date/read-time row, gradient H1 title, rendered MDX body
Footer block: 'Want to talk more about it?' line + solid 'Email me →' pill linking to mailto:hi@silviorodrigues.dev?subject=Re:%20<post title> (URL-encoded)
The Subscribe form/section (from US-7) is repeated below the footer block on this page
Header and Footer (US-2) are present on this route too

userStories.title: Subscribe section and form
userStories.description: As a visitor, I want to subscribe to the newsletter by email, so I get notified of new posts.
acceptanceCriteria: Section #subscribe with gradient H2 'Subscribe 📬' and one-line description
Email input + Subscribe button; client component with state email + status ('idle'|'submitting'|'success'|'error')
On submit: fetch(WORKER_URL, { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ email }) }) where WORKER_URL comes from a public env var (documented, not hardcoded)
On 2xx: swap the form for confirmation message "You're in! Thanks for subscribing 🎉"
On failure: inline error state shown under the input (this state doesn't exist in the HTML reference — this story adds it)
This section is reused as-is on the post detail route (US-6)

userStories.title: Cloudflare Worker for Resend integration
userStories.description: As Silvio, I want a small serverless endpoint that adds emails to my Resend audience, so the static site can have a working subscribe form without a server.
acceptanceCriteria: A worker.js (or worker/ dir) outside the Next.js static bundle implementing a POST handler that validates the email and calls Resend's contacts/audience API using an API key read from Worker environment bindings (never hardcoded)
CORS handling appropriate for the static site's origin
wrangler.toml configured for `wrangler deploy`
Short docs (in the worker directory or README) on required environment variables/secrets and how to deploy — do not actually deploy or require live credentials to complete this story

userStories.title: GitHub Pages deploy workflow
userStories.description: As Silvio, I want pushes to main to publish the static site automatically, so I don't have to deploy by hand.
acceptanceCriteria: GitHub Actions workflow: build the Next.js static export, then actions/deploy-pages, triggered on push to main
Workflow does not attempt to deploy the Cloudflare Worker (that stays a manual/separate `wrangler deploy` per US-8's docs)

userStories.title: Assemble the single-page site and remove old routes
userStories.description: As a visitor, I want everything on one scrolling page matching the design reference, so the browsing experience matches Personal-Website.dc.html.
acceptanceCriteria: app/page.tsx composes Header, Hero (#top), Writing & Projects feed (#work), Subscribe (#subscribe), Footer in that order
No /about, /projects, or /tools routes remain (About and Projects content is folded into the single page per README; Tools page is dropped entirely)
Visual output matches Personal-Website.dc.html and screenshots/*.png for spacing, colors, type and copy (high-fidelity per README — colors/type/spacing/copy are final)

Verified in a real browser via the dev-browser skill or equivalent: load the page, exercise the filter chips, open a post, submit the subscribe form (mock/expected failure is fine without a live Worker), confirm external links open in new tabs

userStories.title: Final QA pass
userStories.description: As Silvio, I want the whole site to pass quality checks and behave correctly end to end before calling this done.
acceptanceCriteria: `npm run lint`, `npm run build` (and typecheck if separate) all pass cleanly
Responsive check at mobile and desktop widths for hero, feed, and subscribe sections
Selection color (#2193b0 bg / #fafafa text) verified
No dead links or console errors on the homepage or a post detail page
All prior stories still pass after this pass (re-verify, don't just trust old commits)
